title: carex sempervirens subsp. firma
intro: Carex sempervirens subsp. firma, commonly known as fir-leaved sedge, is a sub-species of the sedge plant (Carex sempervirens) native to North America. It has been used in traditional medicine for its health benefits, including anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial properties, which may aid in reducing swelling and fighting off infections. The therapeutic actions of fir-leaved sedge include its antioxidant and anti-inflammatory effects, which may help to soothe and calm the body, as well as its potential to support digestive health. The bioactive constituents of Carex sempervirens subsp. firma include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and terpenoids, which are responsible for its medicinal properties.
